clue.text: Not the first young gangster to reach old age

parts.note: what is not first may be second in line
a young person is a child
hood is American slang for a gangster or hoodlum

explanation.surface: A youthful mobster who wasn't the original manages to live to a ripe old age.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes the dotage of the very elderly, when people grow forgetful and dependent like infants.

clue.text: Costa Rica's model politicians?

parts.note: the letters of the first three words rearrange exactly into a party name, and the question mark admits there is no separate signal for it

explanation.surface: The kind of politicians a Central American country holds up as exemplary.
explanation.walkthrough: The fifteen letters of COSTA RICAS MODEL rearrange into the answer; 'model' hints at reshaping, but it is also part of the letters, so the clue works as a cryptic definition with a hidden anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: These are members of centre-left parties combining free elections with welfare-state economics, a fair kind of politician for any country to admire.

clue.text: Hollow cough followed by a smile of embarrassment

indicators.note: a hollow word has its insides emptied, leaving just its first and last letters

parts.note: a broad smile is a grin

explanation.surface: Someone gives a feeble cough then a sheepish smile, plainly embarrassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hollow cough' reads as a medical symptom, but it means the word cough with its middle removed: CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is vexation or mortification at having failed or been humiliated.

clue.text: Define a term to cover "straight"

indicators.note: the words Define a term cover, or contain, the letters of the answer within them

explanation.surface: An instruction to define a term so that it includes the meaning straight.
explanation.definitionFit: A neat whisky is taken straight, with no water or mixer added.

clue.text: Profited from being acquitted

definitions.meaning: a trader who made a net gain of a sum is said to have ... it
a defendant found not guilty is ... of the charge

explanation.surface: Someone made money out of getting off in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the idea of being free: free of costs after a deal, or freed of a criminal charge.

clue.text: Commander in chief trapped in lies about frozen points

indicators.note: one piece is held inside another, like a prisoner caught in a cell
about signals that the letters of lies are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: The head of the armed forces is caught out telling falsehoods about cold spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges LIES into ILES, and 'trapped in' sets CIC inside it after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging spikes of ice taper to sharp tips, so they are pointed formations of frozen water.

clue.text: The obligation of a society girl with time

parts.note: a deb, or debutante, is a young woman making her entrance into high society

explanation.surface: A society girl given time feels the burden of what she owes.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt is money or a favour owed, something one is bound to repay.

clue.text: Japanese art equipment held by old French pal

indicators.note: one piece is gripped inside the other, as if held in someone's arms

parts.note: ami is the French word for a friend
a rig is a set of equipment or apparatus

explanation.surface: An elderly French friend keeps the gear needed for a Japanese craft.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the traditional Japanese craft of folding paper into decorative shapes.

clue.text: Perhaps the exact thing

parts.note: something exact is definite, precise and certain
an article is an object or thing

explanation.surface: Asks whether this might be precisely the right item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps the' looks like a casual opening, but it is the definition: the word 'the' is an example of this grammatical term, signalled by 'Perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'the' is the determiner marking a specific noun, as opposed to 'a' or 'an'.

clue.text: Riddle that church parade leader left

indicators.note: the leading letter of parade has gone away, so its opening P is dropped

explanation.surface: A puzzle about why the man heading a church procession walked off.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is a game where a word is guessed from acted clues to its syllables, a kind of riddle.

clue.text: Where one might put a case, shortly

definitions.text: Where one might put a case
definitions.meaning: a barrister puts a client's case in a brief, the document of instructions from a solicitor

explanation.surface: Explaining briefly where a lawyer might pack a suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal brief holds the case a lawyer argues, and the phrase also means to put something concisely.

clue.text: Publicises a single case of rabies

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single unit

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Broadcasts news of one instance of rabies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of rabies' sounds like a medical instance, but it is the shell of the word: RS.
explanation.definitionFit: To air something is to make it public, as a broadcaster airs a programme.

clue.text: Fee for crossing river to fish

indicators.note: the fee word crosses, or straddles, the river letter so it sits inside

parts.note: a toll is a fee charged for using a road or bridge

explanation.surface: Paying a charge to cross a river so as to go fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: To troll is to angle by trailing a baited line behind a moving boat.

clue.text: North facing pub in farm building

indicators.note: facing puts the north letter beside the pub, so the two sit side by side

parts.note: a bar is a pub or drinking place

explanation.surface: A pub with a northerly aspect in a farmyard building.
explanation.definitionFit: A barn is an agricultural shed used to store hay, grain or livestock.

clue.text: A dangerous escapade is cut short

definitions.meaning: a daring feat such as one performed by a film double
to check or limit growth, as poor diet does to children

explanation.surface: A risky caper is abruptly curtailed.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a risky feat done for show; the other is to hinder growth so something stays undersized.

clue.text: A newly-wed losing right to stay

indicators.note: losing means a letter is dropped from the word for a newly-wed

parts.note: a bride is a woman just married

explanation.surface: A just-married woman forfeits her entitlement to remain.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide is to remain or dwell somewhere, an old word for staying put.

clue.text: Gave teacher wrong date

parts.note: a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters of date are put in a mistaken order

explanation.surface: Someone supplied the schoolteacher with an incorrect date.
explanation.definitionFit: To donate is to give, typically to a charity or cause.

clue.text: Cash advances — one way to survive

parts.note: subs are advance payments on wages, a British usage
I is the Roman numeral for one
ST is the abbreviation for street, a kind of way

explanation.surface: Borrowing against your wages as one method of getting by.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a sub is an advance on pay, so subs are cash advances.
explanation.definitionFit: To subsist is to stay alive, especially on scant means.

clue.text: Mother and child in charge of stonework?

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A mother and her son are running a masonry business.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the adjective really refers to the Freemasons, though it can be read literally as relating to stonemasons.
explanation.definitionFit: Masons are workers in stone, so the adjective formed from them loosely concerns stone building.

clue.text: Emotional individual suffering flu

parts.note: a soul is a person, as in 'not a soul about'

indicators.note: suffering signals the letters of flu being put through distress into a new order

explanation.surface: A person laid low with influenza becomes tearful.
explanation.definitionFit: Something full of deep feeling is described as expressive or moving.

clue.text: Traditional form preceding Inca, oddly

indicators.note: preceding puts the form word in front of the letters taken from Inca

parts.note: a form is a school class

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of the word, first and third

explanation.surface: A traditional shape that came before the Inca civilisation, strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic style is time-honoured and of lasting, accepted excellence.

clue.text: Country road ran all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place signals the letters of road and ran scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A country lane wandered here and there across the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Andorra is a tiny Pyrenean principality between France and Spain.

clue.text: A master glam rock combination

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a degree, so master gives MA

indicators.note: rock signals that the letters of glam are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A skilled glam rock performer blending musical styles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'glam rock' looks like a music genre, but 'rock' is the anagram signal for GLAM, giving LGAM.
explanation.definitionFit: An amalgam is a mixture or blend of different elements.

clue.text: Draft one on time and live below one's station

parts.note: a rough is a preliminary sketch or draft
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Write a first version on schedule and accept a humbler life.
explanation.definitionFit: To live without the usual comforts, as when camping, is to make do with basic conditions.

clue.text: Friend who falls short of being a fool

indicators.note: falls short means the word for a fool loses its final letter

parts.note: a chump is a foolish person

explanation.surface: A pal who isn't quite an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A chum is a close companion or mate.

clue.text: Stories of special forces capturing us state

indicators.note: the special forces seize and hold the state letters inside themselves

parts.note: the SAS is the Special Air Service, the British army's special forces
GA is the postal abbreviation for Georgia, a US state

explanation.surface: Tales of elite troops taking control of an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'us' looks like a pronoun, but read as US it means American: GA, Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagas are long narratives, originally Norse tales of heroic deeds.

clue.text: It's only right

definitions.meaning: fair and equitable, as in 'a fair verdict'

explanation.surface: A simple statement that something is fair and nothing more.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an adverb meaning merely and as an adjective meaning fair or deserved.

clue.text: The final letter in carbon element

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Pointing out the last letter of the word carbon as a chemical element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The final letter in carbon' reads as N, but 'The final letter' is Z, the alphabet's last, and 'in' is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinc is a bluish-white metallic chemical element, used for galvanising.

clue.text: Foreign queen's artist returned home

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a standard abbreviation for an artist

indicators.note: returned means the word for home is read backwards

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: An overseas queen's painter has come back to her house.
explanation.definitionFit: A rani is a Hindu queen or a rajah's wife; the 's stands for 'is'.

clue.text: A female, blonde, soon starts having liaisons

parts.note: fair hair is blonde

indicators.note: starts takes the opening letter of soon

explanation.surface: A blonde woman will soon begin having romantic flings.
explanation.definitionFit: Affairs are romantic or sexual relationships, often illicit ones.

clue.text: Very descriptive of poor/rich gap

indicators.note: poor signals that the letters of rich and gap are badly arranged and need reordering

explanation.surface: A vivid account of the gulf between poor and rich.
explanation.definitionFit: A graphic account is vivid and detailed, sparing nothing.

clue.text: Parliamentarians who choose to send supporter on course

parts.note: to select is to choose
to commit is to send someone, as to prison or to trial
a tee is the peg supporting a golf ball on a golf course

explanation.surface: Members of parliament who decide to dispatch a backer onto a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: These are groups of MPs or peers appointed to scrutinise a particular area of government.
